items.title: Anthropic S-1 Shows Red-Hot Growth, Risks and Massive Computing Costs
items.summary: Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus, reviewed by the Wall Street Journal, discloses an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026 alongside strong revenue growth. The filing also lists a long set of risk factors as the company prepares to go public, and separate reporting says it could spend up to $750 billion on additional computing power in the coming years.
items.why_it_matters: The filing gives the public its first detailed look at the finances behind the AI boom's most valuable private company as it heads toward a market debut.

items.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.summary: Goodfire researcher Nick Cammarata published a 26,000-word blog post arguing he has found good news about the fundamental nature of neural networks, a claim that has sparked widespread speculation and both celebration and skepticism across the AI research community.
items.why_it_matters: A credible new theory about how neural networks actually work could reshape how researchers build and interpret AI systems.

items.title: NScale, Anthropic in Talks for $45B AI Computing Deal
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly in talks with cloud provider Nscale for a computing deal worth up to $45 billion, covering a second facility at Nscale's Monarch data center campus in West Virginia. The site would deliver 460 megawatts of power using Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI chips, and would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year.
items.why_it_matters: It shows how enormous Anthropic's computing needs -- and spending -- have become as it scales its models.

items.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove and stop using products from Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, as well as third-party services built on its technology, citing national security concerns. China has criticized the ban, which also bars future purchases of DeepSeek's products and services.
items.why_it_matters: It marks a significant escalation in the US-China fight over AI dominance and sets a precedent for how Washington treats Chinese AI tools in government.

items.title: AI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’
items.summary: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares, worth about $48 billion at its latest valuation, to a fund for the 'public good' ahead of its planned stock market listing. The move comes amid growing public concern over the safety and economic effects of AI, including fears about job disruption.
items.why_it_matters: It's a high-profile bid by a top AI lab to get ahead of public backlash over AI's economic fallout before going public.

items.title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
items.summary: Google has released a developer tool that lets PyTorch users move their AI apps off Nvidia GPUs, joining Amazon -- whose new TorchNeuron tool lets developers run existing AI code on its Trainium chips without rewriting it. Google separately open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for its TPU chips.
items.why_it_matters: Both moves target Nvidia's grip on the PyTorch ecosystem, a key lever in the broader fight over whose chips run the AI industry.

items.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
items.summary: Security researchers found more than 6,800 publicly accessible links to shared conversations from Meta's Muse AI assistant through public DNS records, exposing users' personal and business secrets. Meta has paused the sharing feature while it investigates, and Royal Bank of Canada's CEO says the bank is considering blocking Muse from accessing its customer data over the risk.
items.why_it_matters: It's a reminder that AI assistants handling sensitive conversations can leak that data in ways users don't expect.

items.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio
items.summary: OpenAI is acquiring biotech startup Orchestra Bio, adding its team and technology to Rosalind, OpenAI's AI model for life sciences research, and to the related Rosalind Workbench tool. The deal is meant to help biopharma teams plan experiments, analyze results and accelerate drug development.
items.why_it_matters: It's another sign of OpenAI pushing beyond chatbots into specialized scientific domains like drug discovery.

items.title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
items.summary: Anthropic has proposed a federal AI safety bill that would allow blocking the release of a model judged capable of killing 50 or more people. But the proposal would actually require a federal agency to get a judge's permission before it could block a model's release, limiting how much power regulators would have.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a leading AI lab trying to shape safety regulation in a way that looks protective but may constrain regulators more than AI developers.

items.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
items.summary: A hacker used a large number of AI agents operating mostly on their own to break into more than 100 websites, according to security firm Norforge. Reuters reports the victims included John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins.
items.why_it_matters: It's an early, concrete example of AI agents being used at scale to automate real-world corporate intrusions.
